description: The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir at Atladra stands on Shastri Yagnapurushdas Marg on the outskirts of Vadodara, Gujarat. It belongs to the Swaminarayan tradition and is run by the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS). According to the sanstha's own pages, Shastriji Maharaj opened it in July 1945 after a devotee from the village gave him land that Swaminarayan is said to have visited. The sanctum area has three shrines: Harikrishna Maharaj with Narayan and Lakshmi, the central shrine of Akshar and Purushottam (Dham, Dhami, Mukta), and a shrine for the Guru Parampara and Sukh Shayya. The mandir hosts weekly assemblies for different age groups and festivals such as Vasant Panchami and Janmashtami.

description: The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Gondal, in Rajkot district of Gujarat, is a temple of the Swaminarayan tradition run by BAPS. It is best known for the Akshar Deri, a shrine marking the cremation place of Gunatitanand Swami, who BAPS followers regard as the first spiritual successor of Swaminarayan. According to Wikipedia, the shrine was built in 1867-68, and a larger temple was later raised around it, with murtis installed in 1934. The complex has several shrines, including Akshar Purushottam in the central sanctum, and Yogi Smruti Mandir, a memorial and museum on the life of Yogiji Maharaj. Devotees perform a daily morning mahapuja at the Akshar Deri, and the shrine was renovated for its 150th anniversary.

description: The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Surat, Gujarat, belongs to the Swaminarayan tradition and is administered by BAPS. According to an older BAPS page about the Surat mandir (which gives a Tapi-bank location near Sardar Bridge, whereas the current BAPS site lists an address at Kanad), its foundation stone was laid on 27 April 1985 by Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the murtis were consecrated on 16 December 1996, after an earlier smaller mandir in the city's Nanavati area, which held murtis brought from the closed Kampala temple in Uganda. The main building has three shrines: Harikrishna Maharaj with Radha-Krishna Dev; Swaminarayan with Gunatitanand Swami and Gopalanand Swami; and Ghanshyam Maharaj. A hostel and weekly devotional gatherings for different age groups operate on site. BAPS describes its mandirs as open to everyone, with modest dress and quiet expected of visitors.

description: The EME Temple, also called the Dakshinamurti Temple, is on the campus of the EME (Electronics and Mechanical Engineers) School of the Indian Army in Vadodara, Gujarat. According to Wikipedia, it was built in February 1966 under the school's first Commandant, and a separate Navgraha shrine was added in 2023. The main deity is Shiva as Dakshinamurti, the teacher facing south. Its modern dome is said to be inspired by Buckminster Fuller's geodesic design, and Wikipedia reports that its elements are meant to reflect several faiths, a claim it marks as needing a citation. The grounds hold a collection of old stone sculptures, about 108 by Wikipedia's count, a replica of the Amarnath linga and a silver arch inscribed Om Namah Shivaya. It is maintained by the Indian Army through the school. Because it lies on a military campus, visitors may need permission or identification to enter.

description: Prabhas Patan, a locality of Veraval in Gir Somnath district, Gujarat, is a pilgrimage town best known for the Somnath Jyotirlinga, and it also has a Shwetambar Jain temple, the Chandraprabh Swami Jain Derasar. According to Wikipedia, the Jain temple lies next to the Daityusudan temple, north of Somnath. Jain pilgrim directories describe the main image as a white Chandraprabhu, the eighth Tirthankara, seated in padmasana, and list the ancient images of Dokadia Parshwanath and Mallinath, an Agam shrine in the basement and a dharamshala. These sources say the place is mentioned in Jain literature as Chandra Prabhas, and attribute the first temple to the legendary emperor Bharat; these accounts are traditional and unverified here. This entry covers only the Chandraprabh Swami Derasar; Jain pilgrim sources mention other temples nearby.

description: Pindara is a village in Kalyanpur taluka of Devbhoomi Dwarka district, on the Gulf of Kutch about eleven miles east of Dwarka. The group consists of five small temples and a long pillared hall inside an enclosure. According to Wikipedia they are dated to the 7th to 10th centuries and are linked with the Saindhava rulers, and locals connect the site with the sage Durvasa. Some shrines are of the Phamsana type with stepped, penthouse-style roofs, and one panel shows the marriage of Shiva and Parvati. The complex is a Monument of National Importance maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India. Offshore, researchers have reported the remains of a submerged temple complex. The Mahabharata lists Pindaraka as a holy bathing place.

description: Bhuj is the main town of Kutch district in Gujarat, and this Swaminarayan temple stands there in the Swaminarayan Sampradaya tradition. According to the temple's own history page and Wikipedia, devotees from Bhuj asked Swaminarayan to have a temple built, and he sent Vaishnavanand Swami with a team of saints; the original building was completed and its images installed in 1823. The January 2001 earthquake badly damaged the old structure, though the images were reported unharmed, and the images were later moved to a new temple a short distance away, inaugurated in 2010. Wikipedia describes the new temple as marble and gold, dedicated to Nar Narayan with Radha Krishna, and associated with the Nar Narayan Dev Gadi.

description: Dholera is a historic port town in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat, about 30 km from Dhandhuka. According to Wikipedia and the Kalupur-branded temple page, this three-domed Swaminarayan temple was planned by senior disciples including Nishkulanand Swami and Atmanand Swami on land gifted by a devotee, Darbar Punjabhai. Swaminarayan is said to have installed the images on 19 May 1826. The central sanctum holds Madan Mohan Dev and Harikrishna Maharaj, with Hanuman and Ganapati near the stairway, and further shrines including Shesh-shayi, Suryanarayan, Dharm-Bhakti, Ghanshyam Maharaj and Shankar-Parvati. Wikipedia counts it among the nine temples built during Swaminarayan's lifetime and says Adbhutanand Swami was appointed its first mahant.

Before construction, the senior saint Ramanand Swami had started a free kitchen (annakshetra) at Jetalpur, served by Gangama, and at her request the temple was built; the images were installed in Vikram Samvat 1882, on the eighth day of the dark half of Falgun. According to Wikipedia, Swaminarayan ordered its construction and Brahmanand Swami supervised the work; the foundation stone was laid on 10 May 1826 and the images were installed on 1 May 1828. Ranchhodrai and Trikamrai are enshrined in the inner sanctum, with Radharaman Dev and Harikrishna Maharaj in the eastern wing and Siddheswar Mahadev, Parvati, Ganesha and Nandishwar on the western side. The building has five spires and many sculptures, and Wikipedia's photo caption mentions a canopy over Swaminarayan's footprints. Wikipedia says Gunatitanand Swami was the first mahant and served in that role for over forty years.

description: The Talaja Caves are a group of rock-cut caves on the hills at Talaja in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat, near the Shetrunji river. They are a Buddhist monastic site; according to Wikipedia, the group has about 30 excavations, roughly half of them water tanks, and the chaitya and cells are dated there to the 2nd century BC, with Jain emblems later added to some cells and halls. The best-known feature is the Ebhal Mandapa, a large hall with octagonal pillars, and the facades carry chaitya-window motifs. Gujarat Tourism says the caves are about 2,000 years old and lie a short walk uphill; the same hill also holds a Jain temple and the Khodiyar Mata temple, so several traditions share the site. Dating is debated, and some historians treat it as uncertain.

description: Caves 30 to 34 form the Jain group of the Ellora rock-cut complex near Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), Maharashtra, a World Heritage Site looked after by the Archaeological Survey of India. Cave 32, the Indra Sabha, has a monolithic elephant in its courtyard facing a tall Manastambha pillar. Caves 32 and 33 (Jagannath Sabha) are linked by a first-floor passage, and the ASI says both retain notable later-period murals. Government tourism text notes the Jain caves hold the most surviving ceiling paintings at Ellora.

description: The Global Vipassana Pagoda is a meditation monument at Gorai, Borivali West, Mumbai, on a peninsula between Gorai creek and the Arabian Sea. According to Wikipedia, it was built entirely from voluntary donations in Burmese style, modelled on the Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon, as thanks to Myanmar and to Sayagyi U Ba Khin for preserving Vipassana, which S. N. Goenka taught in a non-sectarian form. Its central stone dome has no supporting pillars, and the hall is said to seat more than 8,000 meditators. Relics of the Buddha are enshrined in the dome, and the monument was inaugurated in February 2009. The adjoining Dhamma Pattana centre holds ten-day Vipassana courses, offered free of charge, and the complex includes a museum on the Buddha's life.

description: Karla (Karli) lies about 11 km from Lonavala in Maharashtra and holds a group of Buddhist rock-cut shrines and monasteries. According to Wikipedia, they were developed over several centuries, from the 2nd century BCE to the 5th century CE, with donations from local merchants, monks, nuns and rulers supporting the community. The centrepiece is the Great Chaitya hall (Cave 8), which Wikipedia calls the largest and best preserved of its period, notable for its scale and its carved pillars and figures. The caves are a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India. Beside the caves stands the temple of Goddess Ekvira (Ekveera), worshipped especially by the Agri and Koli communities of Mumbai. Local tradition holds that the Pandavas built the temple in a single night during their exile; this is a legend, not a documented history. The temple is a separate, living place of worship.

description: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir stands in the Bhuleshwar area of south Mumbai and belongs to the Swaminarayan Sampraday. According to Wikipedia, a devotee named Ranchhoddas Pranjeevandas first converted his own house into a temple in 1868, and the present three-spired stone building was completed in 1903. The central shrine holds Laxminarayan Dev with Ghanshyam Maharaj, the eastern shrine Radha Golokvihari with Hari Krishna Maharaj, and Shiva, Ganesha and Hanuman are also honoured. Wikipedia notes a carved facade, a flight of steps to the assembly hall, and a dome painted with scenes from Krishna's life. It is listed there as part of the Laxminarayan Dev Gadi based at Vadtal. Festivals include Ram Navami, Janmashtami and Mahashivratri.

description: Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchalnagar Sahib is a gurdwara in Nanded, Maharashtra, on the bank of the Godavari, and one of the five Takhts of the Sikhs. It marks the place where Guru Gobind Singh ji passed away in 1708, after declaring the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru. According to the Takht's own history page, a gurdwara was built on the site between 1832 and 1837 under Maharaja Ranjit Singh. The Takht is administered by the Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchalnagar Sahib Gurdwara Board, Nanded. Its website lists a daily maryada beginning in the early hours with Prakash of Sri Guru Granth Sahib ji, followed by kirtan and katha, and also describes langar, accommodation and other services for visiting sangat.

description: Inside the walls of Jaisalmer Fort in Rajasthan lies a group of seven Shvetambara Jain temples built of local yellow sandstone. According to Wikipedia they are dedicated to the tirthankaras Parshvanatha, Chandraprabha, Rishabhanatha, Sambhavanatha, Shitalanatha, Shantinatha and Kunthunatha, and were established from the 12th century and completed in the 16th. Wikipedia describes the Parshvanatha temple as the oldest, its main shrine ringed by 52 small shrines, and notes a library of manuscripts, the Gyan Bhandar, at the Sambhavanatha temple. The Incredible India tourism page mentions walls carved with animals and human figures and a black-stone image of Parshvanath with a serpent hood canopy. The fort is part of the UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan group.

description: The Kolvi Caves lie near Kolvi village in Jhalawar district, southeastern Rajasthan, cut into a laterite hill. They are a Buddhist rock-cut site, not a Hindu temple. Wikipedia counts about fifty caves and reports that, of 64 monk cells once recorded, the Archaeological Survey of India has verified 45 similar structures. The site includes stupas and chaitya halls with Buddha figures in meditation and standing poses, some with circumambulation paths, and a standing Buddha about twelve feet tall showing the dharmachakra gesture. Wikipedia, citing Cunningham's observations, places the site at about 700 to 900 CE, with the style roughly 8th to 9th century CE,, later than the Bagh and Dhamnar caves, and describes a predominantly Mahayana character. Many figures are weathered, with their faces lost to natural decay.

description: Sanghiji is a Digambar Jain temple in Sanganer, about 16 km from Jaipur, Rajasthan, and a noted pilgrimage site of the tradition. According to Wikipedia, its principal deity is Rishabhanatha (Adinatha), the first Tirthankara, and the idol is traditionally described as extremely ancient. The red-stone temple follows the Nagara style with Maru-Gurjara touches such as carved pillars, bracket figures and lotus ceilings, and has a decorated double-storey entrance and several shikharas. Wikipedia cites a torana inscription dated V.S. 1011 for the final building phase. Its underground levels are said to be kept closed to visitors, and a 1999 account reports that a Jain monk, Muni Sudhasagar, brought out a number of idols from the temple. The shrine is managed by the Shri Digamber Jain Atishaya Kshetra Mandir committee.

description: The Sitaleshwar Temple is a Shiva temple at Jhalrapatan in Jhalawar district, Rajasthan, and belongs to the Chandrabhaga group of temples on the town's edge. According to Wikipedia, the sanctum holds a Shiva lingam with a Nandi facing it in the hall, and the temple was built in the 7th century with its pillared hall added in the 10th. It faces east and has a hall, an antechamber and a square sanctum. The original tower collapsed, leaving a flat roof with a small dome. The pillars are carved with female figures, directional guardians and ascetics, and the sanctum doorway shows Ganga and Yamuna and Lakulisa in the lintel. It is listed as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.

description: The Tijara Jain temple (Chandraprabhu Atishaya Kshetra) is a Digambar Jain temple at Dehra in Tijara town, in the Khairthal-Tijara district (formerly Alwar) of Rajasthan, and is regarded as an atishaya kshetra, a pilgrimage place associated with miracles. It is dedicated to Chandraprabhu, the eighth Tirthankara. According to Wikipedia, the temple was established after an idol of Chandraprabha was recovered from the ground on 16 August 1956, and a second small idol was found in 1972, which supported the belief that the site had long been a dehra. The principal image is a white marble Chandraprabhu with an inscription dated 1497 CE. The complex has a manastambha, a Chandragiri Vatika, and shrines to Parshvanatha, Padmavati and the Navagraha.
